About this training

A closed-circuit rebreather recycles your breathing gas, removing carbon dioxide and adding oxygen so almost nothing is wasted. The result is dramatically longer dives, warm moist gas and near-silent, bubble-free presence in the water.

Rebreather training is a progression in its own right, independent of any overhead environment. You start with the fundamentals of the loop and build through decompression and mixed-gas diving, with cave-specific CCR work as an later specialism for those who want it. I teach on both the KISS Sidewinder and the AP Inspiration, so you train on the unit you intend to dive.

Prerequisites

  • Nitrox certification
  • Solid buoyancy and experience
  • Commitment to checklists
  • Medically fit to dive

What you will build

01

Loop understanding

Learn how the counterlungs, scrubber and cells work together to keep you breathing.

02

PO2 monitoring

Track and manage your oxygen partial pressure so the loop stays inside safe limits.

03

Bail-out discipline

Rehearse switching to open-circuit bail-out until it becomes an instinctive response.

Course progression

Training is delivered in stages, so you can progress at a pace that keeps every skill solid before moving deeper.

1

CCR Air Diluent

ESTIMATED: 8 DAYS // LEVEL 1 ENTRY

Unit Focus: KISS Sidewinder & AP Inspiration Platforms. Industry Pathway: TDI Air Diluent / PADI Tec CCR Basics (Mod 1 No-Deco). Shifting completely away from open-circuit muscle memory to master real-time loop mechanics, unit assembly, and execution of pre-dive checklists with strict personal discipline.

  • Unit assembly and strict pre-dive checklist execution
  • Real-time diluent and oxygen loop management metrics
  • Bail-out to open circuit safety protocols
  • Buoyancy and precise horizontal trim on a closed loop
2

CCR Air Diluent Decompression

ESTIMATED: 8 DAYS // TECH DIVER ENTRY

Unit Focus: KISS Sidewinder & AP Inspiration Platforms. Industry Pathway: TDI Air Diluent Decompression / PADI Tec 40 CCR (Mod 1 Deco). Direct entry path for open-circuit technical divers or a clean upgrade track for Level 1 CCR divers looking to advance their loop operational skills.

  • Advanced loop electronics tracking and monitoring
  • Planning and executing staged decompression obligations
  • Deco gas transitions and bail-out management protocols
  • Handling loop failure diagnostics under a decompression penalty
3

CCR Mixed Gas & Trimix

ESTIMATED: 6 DAYS // LEVEL 2 PROGRESSION

Unit Focus: KISS Sidewinder & AP Inspiration Platforms. Industry Pathway: TDI Mixed Gas / PADI Tec 60 CCR (Mod 2). Advanced training for certified decompression rebreather divers looking to integrate Helium into their rebreather loop architecture.

  • Trimix diluent planning and gas density control metrics
  • Managing multiple open-circuit technical bail-out logistics
  • Extended decompression profiling and oxygen exposure limits
  • Deep-water dive logistics and multi-stage execution profiles
4

CCR Cave Cross-Over

ESTIMATED: 5 DAYS // OVERHEAD CROSS-OVER

Unit Focus: Open to any active CCR platform architecture. This intensive pathway is designed exclusively for certified, active Open Circuit Full Cave Divers looking to safely transition their established overhead navigation and air-sharing protocols onto a closed-circuit loop loop.

  • Adapting open-circuit cave muscle memory to closed-circuit boundaries
  • Unit-specific overhead failure management and emergency loop safety rules
  • Complex rebreather bail-out mechanics and gas-matching execution profiles
  • TDI certified overhead crossing parameters across all local systems
5

TDI CCR Cave Progression

ESTIMATED: 10 DAYS // COMPLETE OVERHEAD TRACK

Unit Focus: Open to any active CCR platform architecture. Curriculum Pathway: TDI CCR Cavern // TDI CCR Intro to Cave // TDI CCR Full Cave. A comprehensive, non-negotiable linear progression for rebreather divers with no prior cave experience, built around developing strict survival habits in total darkness.

  • Linear 3-course track from initial cavern limits to full cave navigation
  • Mastering real-time loop tracking safety boundaries under severe task-loading
  • Silt-out exit drills, touch-contact team routines, and emergency protocols
  • Complex route navigation managing jumps, gaps, and circuit planning
